section_summary.extract_value: This Discussion section presents findings from a single study examining how self-compassion buffers the relationship between daily interactions with body-focused others and body image/eating outcomes among college women. The study employed a within-persons and between-persons design, revealing that higher-than-usual self-compassion on specific days protected against negative effects of body-focused interactions, and that women with higher overall self-compassion were less negatively affected by frequent interactions with body-focused others. The findings suggest that self-compassion may be particularly protective against diet- and body-focused talk, but less critical when exposure involves exercise-focused interactions.
